name: On the Nature of Undeath
description: A forbidden text, its cover bound in something not quite leather.
paragraphs: Death is not a wall but a door, and doors -- as any locksmith will tell you -- can be forced. The necromancer does not create life where there was none; he merely refuses to let go of what remains.

The Church calls this an abomination. The Church has never had to watch someone it loved be taken by the plague. I do not ask forgiveness for my work. I ask only that it be remembered why it was begun.
Those who follow this path further than I did should know: the dead do not forget what was done to bring them back. Sooner or later, they ask why.
